acceptance.output_evidence:
RECORDED FOR 3.0.0_SA_CVO AT L9. NO VERDICT IS OFFERED.

1. WHAT A SCHEDULED FIRE CAN DO THAT THE DRIVEN FIRE DID NOT.

   THE CLOCK. Every driven fire in this cell supplied `business_date` on the event. A scheduled
   fire supplies none and `lambda_handler` reads `dt.date.today()` -- the ONE place in the module
   that touches a clock, asserted by a test that walks the AST. So the scheduled fire's business
   date is a fact no harness here has exercised: on Monday 2026-09-14 at 13:00Z the fire will
   compute `today()` in UTC inside a Lambda, while the SCHEDULE's cadence is pinned to
   America/New_York. A fire at 09:00 New York in January is 14:00Z and in July 13:00Z; neither
   crosses a UTC date boundary, so the two agree today -- but nothing in this cell PROVES that,
   and a schedule whose expression is zoned while its handler's clock is not is a real seam.

   THE HOST'S OWN STATE. The driven fires all found the runner `running` and SSM `Online`,
   because another cell had already started it and amendment H7 forbade stopping it. A 13:00Z
   scheduled fire will usually find it STOPPED: the mdpf daily chain starts the box at 15:00Z and
   stops it at the end of its own run, so at 09:00 New York the box is most likely down. The
   dispatcher then issues ONE `ec2:StartInstances` and ENDS -- it does not wait -- and records
   REFRESH_FAILED with HAND_OVER_RUNNER_OFFLINE. The next fire, a day later, finds a host that has
   had time to come up only if something kept it up; the mdpf chain will have stopped it again. SO
   THE SCHEDULED PATH HAS A LIFECYCLE HOLE THIS CELL DOES NOT CLOSE, and closing it means either
   waiting inside the function (refused by amendment H4) or owning a lifecycle the mdpf chain
   already owns (refused by the accrual bridge's own reasoning: a refresh that shut the box down
   could kill a chain run mid-flight). It is stated here rather than papered over.

   A CONCURRENT mdpf RUN. The refresh dispatches three commands, one per firm, into a host the
   mdpf daily chain shares. They unpack into /tmp under per-(firm, date) directories and touch
   nothing the chain uses, and at 13:00Z they do not overlap the chain's 15:00Z window -- but
   `AWS-RunShellScript` commands on one instance are not serialised by SSM, so three directory
   builds plus a catch-up chain run could contend for the same box's CPU and memory. Nothing in
   this cell measures that, and no arm here was run while the chain was running.

2. HOW A FAILED SSM DISPATCH IS DISTINGUISHED FROM A FAILED BUILD IN THE ENVELOPE.

   THE ENVELOPE DOES NOT DISTINGUISH THEM, DELIBERATELY, AND THE MANIFEST DOES. Both are
   REFRESH_FAILED with state FAILED, because both mean the same thing to a reader of the envelope:
   this fire produced no directory. `public_reason_code` is a CODE and never a message, and
   widening the envelope's vocabulary to carry an operator's diagnosis would put plumbing in a
   contract the counterpart parses.

   THE MANIFEST BESIDE IT CARRIES WHICH, from a CLOSED token set derived by subtraction over a
   printed denominator (6 `raise DispatchError` sites, 5 tokens; the two numbers differ for exactly
   one stated reason -- HAND_OVER_NOT_CONFIGURED covers a missing instance id and a missing bundle
   uri, the same failure with two spellings):
     HAND_OVER_NOT_CONFIGURED / HAND_OVER_RUNNER_OFFLINE / HAND_OVER_RUNNER_UNSTARTABLE
        -> OURS. The build was never handed over. `build_dispatch_half` = HAND_OVER.
     BUILD_ENDED_UNSUCCESSFUL
        -> THE RUNNER'S. The command WAS accepted and ended other than Success.
           `build_dispatch_half` = BUILD, and `build_command_status` carries AWS's own status.
     BUILD_STATUS_UNREADABLE
        -> NEITHER, and it must never silently become "still running".
   MEASURED IN PRODUCTION, not asserted: the 2026-09-11 fire that read back a failed command wrote
   to opal-data-bd delta {"build_command_status": "Failed", "build_dispatch_failure":
   "BUILD_ENDED_UNSUCCESSFUL", "build_dispatch_half": "BUILD", "build_error": "DispatchError"}.
   `detail` carries the AWS status and nothing else -- no exception text, no source value, no key.

   A THIRD STATE EXISTS AND IS NOT A FAILURE: REFRESH_DISPATCHED / RUNNING / WAIT, for a fire whose
   build is in flight. Its action is WAIT and NEVER RETRY, because re-firing while a command is in
   flight double-dispatches onto a shared host. The CVO may wish to grade whether a closed
   vocabulary gaining a member mid-round is the right call; the four-postulate record and the
   word-boundary census (REFRESH_DISPATCHED -> 0 hits across 31,448 files) are in expiry.py beside
   the member, and the frozen v1 contract was read before the edit: `public_reason_code` is typed
   string with pattern ^[A-Z0-9_]+$ and carries NO enum, while the contract's `state` enum ALREADY
   carried RUNNING.

3. WHAT THE AS-OF AN ADVISOR READS NOW MEASURES.

   NOTHING YET, AND THAT IS THE HONEST ANSWER. There is no directory artifact in any of the three
   firm buckets -- `list-objects-v2` on investor-reporting/directory/ returns 0 directory.json and
   0 latest.json for 3 of 3 firms -- so no advisor can read an as-of at all today. What EXISTS is
   the freshness accounting: three `_refresh/<date>/manifest.json` objects saying a fire happened,
   what it handed over, and what came back.

   WHEN AN ARTIFACT DOES LAND, the as-of an advisor reads will measure THE SOURCE'S COMPLETION,
   never the clock and never the fire. `new_manifest` takes `source_completion_date` from the
   build's own completion manifest, and directory_runner.py chooses its business date by walking
   the trading calendar back until EVERY source that firm needs has a COMPLETED partition at or
   before the candidate. So a directory written at 09:00 for a T-1 build says T-1. A manifest that
   recorded its write time would make every run look fresh, which is the defect this shape avoids.

   AND ONE SEAM THE CVO SHOULD SEE. This cell CHANGED what the manifest's own
   `as_of_business_date` means: it is now THE FIRE'S date, not the artifact's, because the build is
   asynchronous and the two are no longer the same value. The artifact's date travels as
   `delta.artifact_business_date` and in the envelope's `source_dates.business_date`. Any consumer
   that read `as_of_business_date` off a manifest as "the date of the directory" would now be
   reading "the date of the fire". No such consumer exists today (the `_refresh/` prefix was empty
   in all three buckets before this cell), which is why the change was safe to make -- but it is a
   meaning change and it is named here rather than left for someone to discover.
